transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood CSM) — Alex Park (CTO), Lina Gomez (Lead DevOps), Priya Nair (Product), Tom Sullivan (Security), Jared Osei (Eng Lead)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for implementation and intake. Pilot recommended on Dedicated capacity with VPC peering; collect network details and KPIs; schedule technical deep dive for bench runs.

[00:00] Emily Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Emily from Redwood, AE for Cardinal. Quick intros — Mateo with me from SE and Sanjay from success. Can we go around on your side?
[00:10] Alex Park: Hi, Alex here, CTO. We're excited to move from eval to pilot.
[00:16] Lina Gomez: Lina, Lead DevOps — I'll own network and infra.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya, product — focusing on user-facing latency and safety checkpoints.
[00:24] Tom Sullivan: Tom, security. I'll be the compliance reviewer.
[00:28] Jared Osei: Jared, eng lead for the ingestion and realtime features.
[00:33] Mateo Ruiz: Great, thanks. Outline for today: confirm success criteria/KPIs, collect network intake details, align pilot timeline, and call out outstanding security asks.

[02:05] Emily: Alex, you mentioned p95 targets in the email. Can you restate what success looks like for you?
[02:14] Alex: Yeah — p95 under 200ms for typical 256 token responses for synchronous chat flows; for batch generation we want cost below about $0.001/token ideally, but we can be flexible. Also need predictable 99.9% uptime during business hours.
[02:36] Emily: Good. Mateo — in most cases Dedicated capacity gives predictable p95s, and caching/prefix reuse can help with cost. We'll show a config that targets those numbers.

[04:10] Lina: On network, we have a restrictive egress policy. We need to know your egress IPs, TLS requirements, and whether we can route through an outbound proxy. Also what ports and IP ranges for VPC peering?
[04:25] Mateo: Totally. We have static egress ranges for hosted and for dedicated we publish potential egress ranges; for Private we can do no-egress setups. We'll send the allowlist template. Note: sometimes our docs call this Redwood Privy in error — sorry, that's Redwood Private.

[06:00] Tom: SOC2 is a blocker for our procurement. We need SOC2 Type II report and details on audit log retention. Also SSO, SAML, RBAC for admin. How does key management work?
[06:15] Emily: We have SOC2 material in the security pack. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments; for hosted we support customer KMS via token wrapping—we'll include options. Audit logs are configurable; retention tiers are an add-on.

[08:40] Priya: For product, we're concerned about quality regression during model rollouts. How do you support prompt versioning and comparative evals?
[08:52] Mateo: Redwood Optimize supports evals tied to prompt sets. You can run A/B rollouts and automatic rollback if quality drops. We'll demo the rollout UI in the next deep dive. Note: sometimes the transcriber writes 'quantize Asian' instead of quantization — ignore that.

[11:30] Jared: For the staging pilot, what does the canonical deployment look like? Do we point our API gateway at Redwood or do you sit behind our VPC?
[11:42] Mateo: Two main patterns: 1) For quick start you call our hosted API over TLS with allowlisted egress IPs; 2) For stricter isolation use Dedicated with VPC peering or Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane. We'll recommend Dedicated with VPC peering for your pilot to match production networking.

[14:05] Alex: Cost question — how is burst capacity billed? We have periodic spikes due to nightly batch jobs.
[14:15] Emily: Dedicated includes a base reservation; burst is metered at a higher rate. We'll include projected estimates for your expected QPS and token volume. If bursts are frequent, a higher baseline is often cheaper.

[16:00] Tom: Security follow-ups: do you support encryption in transit and at rest with our KMS? Can we get a SOC scoping call?
[16:12] Sanjay: Yes, encryption is standard. We'll set up a SOC scoping session with our security engineer. Expect a short questionnaire first.

[18:20] Emily: Timeline proposal — 6 week pilot: week 1 network intake and staging setup, week 2-3 benchmark and tuning, week 4-5 integration and safety tests, week 6 go/no-go demo and rollout plan. Thoughts?
[18:36] Alex: That's reasonable. We want the demo to use production-like traffic patterns.
[18:45] Mateo: We'll provide a benchmark harness and a sample prompt set. Please include your top 10 intents and any long-form documents users often send — that affects KV cache size and memory.

[21:00] Lina: About IPs — we require static egress through our firewall. Will Redwood accept connections from our side or do you need us to open ports to your egress?
[21:14] Mateo: We can do either. For VPC peering you open our CIDR on your side and we peer into your VPC. For hosted API you need to allow our egress IPs. We'll send both templates.

[23:30] Priya: On observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards. Is that available?
[23:40] Sanjay: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token cost breakdown and tracing hooks. We'll give you a sample dashboard and we can add custom widgets for your routes.

[25:50] Jared: A couple of gotchas we hit earlier: we use a autoscaling lambda-based ingestion that does short-lived connections; how do you manage long-lived KV cache?
[26:05] Mateo: We handle KV cache on the serving side; short-lived clients are fine. We'll outline best practices for continuous batching and TTL policies. Some docs might say 'key V cache' in transcripts but we mean KV cache.

[28:30] Tom: For compliance, can we restrict who can access logs and have RBAC tied to our SAML provider?
[28:40] Emily: Yes, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for RBAC is supported in the enterprise plan. We'll include an onboarding checklist for SAML attributes.

[31:00] Alex: Competitors — we've looked at VendorX and BigCloud; we like Redwood's runtime optimizations and cost controls, but will want to validate latency in our environment.
[31:18] Emily: Understood. We'll propose a perf run and share comparable numbers from similar customers as a baseline.

[33:40] Mateo: Technical deep dive items to prep: network diagram, sample traffic shape (QPS, p50/p95 requirements), prompt list with distribution of sequence lengths, and whether you need on-prem later.
[33:55] Lina: We'll produce the topology and the list of egress devices. One question: do you support proxy chaining?
[34:05] Mateo: Yes, through outbound proxies we can route; just note latency overhead. We'll mark that in the perf checklist.

[36:30] Priya: On rollout strategy: we want canary 10% then 50% then 100% with automatic rollback on quality regressions. Does Redwood support that?
[36:41] Sanjay: Yes, rollouts with automatic fallback based on eval metrics are supported. We should align on which eval metrics trigger rollback.

[38:20] Alex: One last item — data residency. Some clients require Europe-only processing for PII. Do you have multi-region controls?
[38:35] Emily: Yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have region options but less isolation. We'll note that for your account.

[41:00] Emily: Let's recap next steps: we'll send network allowlist template, security pack, and dedicated pricing + SOW. You'll share network topology, traffic shape, and prompts. We'll schedule a 60m deep-dive for bench runs.
[41:20] Alex: Sounds good. Who will own the SOW?
[41:25] Emily: I'll own SOW and price, Mateo will own technical bench and tuning.

[43:00] Tom: Minor transcription note — in some exports proper nouns are off. We will rely on the docs not the verbatim transcript for compliance.
[43:10] Sanjay: Understood. We'll make sure security docs are explicit.

[45:00] Jared: Quick question about retention and prompt audit — if we want to log prompts for QA, can we mask PII automatically?
[45:12] Mateo: Yes, Redwood can optionally redact or hash PII before storing. We have an integration guide.

[47:40] Priya: For the pilot, do you expect we need a dedicated engineer from Redwood onsite?
[47:50] Emily: Not onsite — but weekly syncs and a couple of working sessions with the SE is typical. We can add extra SE time if you want a tighter SLA.

[50:00] Alex: Ok final check — timeline dependency: we need network and security reviewers cleared by 2026-12-20 to hit an internal demo on 2027-01-10.
[50:10] Emily: We'll aim for that. I'll send the documents by 2026-12-13 and propose dec-16 deep dive.

[52:30] Lina: Thanks team. One small ask: include sample firewall rules in CIDR format in the allowlist doc.
[52:40] Mateo: Will do.

[54:00] Emily: Great, thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pack and action items.
[54:10] Alex: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
